questions.text: Under Section 705, what source controls the allowable maximum TGFA of a proposed building or structure?

options.text: Rule VII of the 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096
The designer's preferred floor area ratio only
A fixed national value regardless of occupancy

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Rule VII of the 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 705.

questions.text: In Table VII.1, what do the numbers 3, 5, 12, 18, and 30 represent?

options.text: Storeys or floors, not percentage values

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Storeys or floors, not percentage values. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 705.

questions.text: After allowable maximum TGFA is initially established, what control must it be crosschecked against?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Allowable Maximum Volume of Building (AMVB). This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 705.

questions.text: If the allowable maximum TGFA exceeds the AMVB, what happens under Section 705?

options.text: The maximum allowable TGFA must be adjusted because AMVB prevails
Only the building permit fee changes

questions.rationale: Correct answer: The maximum allowable TGFA must be adjusted because AMVB prevails. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 705.

questions.text: Under Section 706, what site condition can support an allowable floor area increase?

options.text: Public space, streets, or yards extending along and adjoining two or more sides of the building or structure
Any one interior partition facing a corridor
A private stair serving one tenant

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Public space, streets, or yards extending along and adjoining two or more sides of the building or structure. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 706.
questions.explanation: When the open-space width reaches the 30-foot cap, the frontage formula no longer rewards additional width. The simplified result keeps the frontage-to-perimeter ratio and subtracts the 0.25 threshold, so “If = F/P − 0.25” is the defensible answer. The other choices either multiply by the cap, reverse the subtraction, or omit the threshold.

questions.text: Whose approval is required for a Section 706 allowable floor area increase?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: The Building Official. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 706.

questions.text: After allowable maximum TGFA is initially established, what control must it be crosschecked against?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Allowable Maximum Volume of Building (AMVB). This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 705.
questions.explanation: The AMBF = TLA × PSO formula is the starting point for all building footprint calculations. A slender tower can have a small PSO (small footprint) but a high FLAR (many stacked floors). These are two independent simultaneous controls on building size.
questions.code_citation: 2004 Revised IRR, Guidelines on Determining GFA

questions.text: If the allowable maximum TGFA exceeds the AMVB, what happens under Section 705?

options.text: The maximum allowable TGFA must be adjusted because AMVB prevails
Only the building permit fee changes

questions.rationale: Correct answer: The maximum allowable TGFA must be adjusted because AMVB prevails. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 705.
questions.explanation: Option B is the most common wrong answer — 'one side' is insufficient. The provision requires 'two or more sides.' The rationale is that multi-sided frontage provides more effective fire separation from neighboring structures, reducing the cumulative fire risk that justifies floor area limits.

questions.explanation: These PSO values for Group A are higher than those for other residential occupancy groups. The confusion arises because in other groups, corner lots also receive higher allowances, but at lower absolute values. For Group A specifically, Section 708 establishes these high coverage percentages reflecting the low-rise, high-density character of Filipino residential neighborhoods.

questions.text: Whose approval is required for a Section 706 allowable floor area increase?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: The Building Official. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 706.
questions.explanation: For a multi-story building with If = 0.75 and Is = 2.00, additive gives At + 0.75At + 2.00At = 3.75At. The multiplicative approach would give At × 1.75 × 3.00 = 5.25At — a 40% overstatement. The IBC explicitly uses additive form to prevent double-compounding of two independent safety bonuses.

questions.text: How should a reviewer treat Section 706 in an exam problem?

options.text: As a conditional increase subject to stated site conditions and Building Official approval
As a guaranteed increase for every corner lot
As unrelated to public space, streets, or yards

questions.rationale: Correct answer: As a conditional increase subject to stated site conditions and Building Official approval. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 706.
questions.explanation: Option D (same factor for both) is the most common error. The distinction between single-story and multi-story sprinkler bonuses reflects fire physics: in a single-story building, sprinklers suppress the fire in the horizontal plane with no vertical complications. The 1.00-point difference between Is = 2.00 and Is = 3.00 is significant in combined area calculations.

questions.text: Under Section 707, which building-height rule applies when the local zoning ordinance is more restrictive than Rule VII?

options.text: The local zoning ordinance controls because the more restrictive limit applies
Rule VII always overrides local zoning

questions.rationale: Correct answer: The local zoning ordinance controls because the more restrictive limit applies. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 707.
questions.explanation: Option C reverses the two systems. The PH system's flexibility (discretionary Building Official review) allows context-specific judgment. The IBC system's certainty (formula-derived result) provides predictability. Developers working under the IBC can calculate allowable area with confidence before submitting plans.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096, Rule VII, Sec. 706; IBC 2021, Sec. 506.4

questions.text: Under Section 705, what source controls the allowable maximum TGFA of a proposed building or structure?

options.text: Rule VII of the 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096
The designer's preferred floor area ratio only
A fixed national value regardless of occupancy

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Rule VII of the 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 705.
questions.explanation: The 0.25 threshold is the qualifying floor — below it, no increase. The 0.75 cap prevents the frontage bonus from dominating the calculation. Both are hard limits that must be memorized. The simplified form when W = 30 ft (the cap): If = F/P − 0.25.

questions.text: In Table VII.1, what do the numbers 3, 5, 12, 18, and 30 represent?

options.text: Storeys or floors, not percentage values

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Storeys or floors, not percentage values. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 705.
questions.explanation: Option A (0.25) is the threshold — forgetting to subtract it from F/P. Option B (0.60) is the raw F/P ratio — forgetting the subtraction entirely. Option D (0.75) is the maximum cap. Converting meters to feet for W, applying the 30 ft cap, computing F/P correctly, and subtracting 0.25 are all required steps.
